notes: Items PF01 to PF12 are the Appendix C seed items (rationales added where the spec gave none). Items PF13 to PF24 were written for this build in the same style (C.5 task 5). Clause tags are references only and are unverified against the purchased standard. clause2015 holds the primary clause; clauseRefs lists every clause the spec or author cited. Spec pack prefix PF maps to pack id "process-food".

items.stem: The label artwork on the packaging line is the previous revision. What should happen?
options: Stop the run, hold the product already labeled, and obtain the current approved artwork.
Cover the difference with a sticker.
Ask the line operator to decide.
items.rationale: Obsolete documents are not used, and affected output is controlled.

items.stem: A temperature probe used to verify processing has no verification record for the required interval. What is the proper response?
options: Stop using it, flag it, and assess the validity of earlier readings.
items.rationale: Measurement validity depends on verification at defined intervals.

items.stem: A laboratory result needed for batch release is still pending at the end of shift. What should happen?
options: The batch remains on hold until the result is reviewed and release is authorized.
Release it on the supervisor's estimate.
items.rationale: Release follows completion of planned verification.

items.stem: A customer supplies its own printed packaging. A pallet arrives with water damage. Which action is correct?
options: Use the dry boxes and discard the rest quietly.
Use all of it; it is only packaging.
Identify and protect the packaging, record the damage, and inform the customer.
items.rationale: Damaged customer property is reported to the customer and records are retained.

items.stem: A customer complaint concerns one batch. Which capability limits the scope of a review or recall?
options: Batch identification and traceability to ingredient and packaging lots.
items.rationale: Traceability records link outputs to inputs and process steps.

items.stem: An ingredient arrives past the date by which the supplier states it should be used. What is the best action?
options: Use it first because it is aging.
Accept it if the driver agrees.
Do not use it; hold it, identify it, and follow the nonconformance procedure.
items.rationale: Nonconforming inputs are identified and controlled.

items.stem: A process parameter is changed to improve yield. What is required?
options: Review of consequences, authorization, communication, and records.
An informal note on the shift sheet.
Only the supervisor needs to know.
items.rationale: Changes are reviewed and controlled.

items.stem: A new operator has not been qualified on the filling step. What does the organization need before independent work?
options: Allow it if a colleague is nearby.
Allow it if the shift is busy.
Competence determined, training provided, and evidence retained.
items.rationale: People are competent for their work, and evidence of competence is retained.

items.stem: The same labeling error recurs monthly. Retraining operators each time has not solved it. What should be done?
options: Find the underlying cause in the system (instruction, tooling, workload, checks) and act on it.
items.rationale: Corrective action addresses the cause, not only the symptom.

items.stem: Which input does management review normally consider?
options: Customer feedback, process performance, nonconformities, audit results, and provider performance.
items.rationale: These are among the inputs that management review is expected to consider.

items.stem: A supervisor proposes shipping a batch with an unresolved labeling discrepancy because the truck is waiting. What is the right response?
options: Hold the batch until the discrepancy is resolved or release is authorized as required.
Ship it; the truck is waiting.
Relabel on the truck without a record.
items.rationale: Release proceeds only when requirements are verified or release is authorized.

items.stem: Quality objectives should be:
options: Measurable, consistent with the policy, monitored, and communicated.
items.rationale: Objectives give direction only when they can be measured, are aligned with the policy, and are tracked and shared.

items.stem: A retail customer announces that it will require recyclable packaging from next year. Where should Meridian Foods first take account of this?
options: In its review of external issues and interested-party requirements that affect its system and planning.
Nowhere; retailer plans are not relevant.
items.rationale: External issues and the relevant requirements of interested parties are monitored and reviewed, and they feed planning.

items.stem: On-time delivery has fallen for several months, but no customer has complained formally. What does customer focus expect of leadership?
options: Make sure customer requirements are determined and met, and act on risks to customer satisfaction.
items.rationale: Top management demonstrates customer focus by keeping customer requirements and satisfaction at the center of decisions.

items.stem: An operator is asked what the quality policy means for the packaging line. Which answer shows awareness?
options: "I do not need to know it."
"It is on the wall in the office."
"It commits us to meeting customer requirements, so I check labels and codes against the approved specification."
items.rationale: People are aware of the quality policy and can relate it to their own work.

items.stem: A long-serving technician knows a changeover sequence that is not written down anywhere. What should the organization do?
options: Capture the knowledge so it is maintained and available, for example in an instruction or in training.
Ask the technician never to leave.
Keep it confidential to the technician.
items.rationale: The organization determines the knowledge needed for its processes and keeps it available.

items.stem: The only filling machine has no backup and has failed twice this quarter. What is a proportionate planning response?
options: Assess the risk to deliveries and conformity, plan actions such as spare parts or a revised maintenance plan, and review whether they worked.
items.rationale: Actions to address risks are proportionate to the potential effect, and their effectiveness is evaluated.

items.stem: The lighting in the packing area is too dim to read batch codes reliably. Which requirement area is most relevant?
options: Environment for the operation of processes.
items.rationale: The organization provides and maintains the conditions needed for its processes, including physical factors such as lighting.

items.stem: An entry on a batch record has been covered with correction fluid, with no initials or date. What is the concern?
options: Changes to the record are not controlled, so it may not be trustworthy evidence.
items.rationale: Retained records are protected from unintended alteration, and changes are controlled and traceable.

items.stem: A new customer asks for a different pack size and case configuration. Before the order is accepted, what should be confirmed?
options: That the requirements, including any the customer did not state but that are needed, are determined and can be met.
items.rationale: Requirements for products are determined, including those needed for intended use, before the organization commits to supply.

items.stem: The reject bin on the checkweigher is unlocked, and rejected packs can be returned to the line. What is the concern?
options: Controls meant to keep rejected output out of the product flow can be bypassed.
items.rationale: Controlled conditions include measures that prevent nonconforming output from rejoining conforming product.

items.stem: After delivery, a customer asks for support with a question about the packaging of a batch. Which requirement area covers this?
items.rationale: The organization meets agreed requirements for activities after delivery, such as customer support.

items.stem: The plant tracks many indicators but has not decided which ones show whether processes achieve their planned results. What is missing?
options: A decision on what to monitor and measure, how, when, and when the results are analyzed.
items.rationale: The organization decides what needs monitoring and measurement and how the results will be evaluated.

items.stem: An internal auditor asks an operator to show how she checks label codes. What is the best response?
options: Say what she thinks the auditor wants to hear.
Show the actual practice and the record, and say so honestly if unsure.
Send the auditor to the supervisor without answering.
items.rationale: Audits rely on accurate evidence of actual practice; honest answers help the organization improve.
